sources.entry: DietPi - Minimal Debian OS optimized for single-board computers, which allows you to easily install and manage several services for selfhosting at home. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 Shell

summary.one_liner: DietPi is a lightweight Debian-based OS for single-board computers, with Bash-based tools to install and manage self-hosted services.
summary.what_it_does: DietPi is a minimal Debian-based operating system aimed at single-board computers, tuned for low CPU and RAM usage. The dietpi-software tool installs preconfigured applications (the README lists desktops, remote desktop, media servers, torrent clients, cloud and backup, home automation, webserver stacks, Pi-hole, file servers, printing and more) and sets them up, including starting services. dietpi-config provides a whiptail-based configuration menu, and dietpi-services adjusts nice, affinity and scheduler priorities for installed software. dietpi-update checks for and applies updates without re-flashing the image. DietPi can be fully automated from an unattended install by editing dietpi.txt before first boot. The project is written entirely in Bash scripts with no build step.
use_cases: run a home server on a Raspberry Pi or similar board
install self-hosted apps with a menu-driven tool
set up Pi-hole or a file server on a single-board computer
automate unattended OS installs on SBCs
run a home automation hub on minimal hardware
manage service priorities on a low-resource device
how_to_run: Download a DietPi image for your board from the project website and write it to an SD card or drive
Boot the device and follow the first-run setup
Run dietpi-config to adjust system settings
Run dietpi-software to choose and install applications
Optionally edit dietpi.txt before first boot for automated installation
notable: Ready-to-run application installer (dietpi-software) that performs the configuration automatically
Unattended installation driven by a dietpi.txt file
Lightweight whiptail menus instead of raw command line work
In-place updates via dietpi-update without writing a new image
Pure Bash codebase with no compilation required
caveats: Designed for single-board computers; the README names specific boards (RPi, Odroid, Orange Pi, NanoPi, Radxa, PINE64) and does not cover general desktop hardware
Relies on a Debian base and custom DietPi tooling rather than standard distribution packaging
The README does not state platform support limits beyond the listed boards
keywords: lightweight alternative to raspberry pi os
